sents.t: For Lily’s birthday in September, I surprised her with a trip to New Orleans.
She has always dreamed of tasting the food there.
New Orleans was founded by the French in 1718, and it feels different from any other American city.
In the French Quarter, the old houses are painted in bright colors and decorated with iron balconies full of flowers.
Music is played on almost every corner.
On our first morning, we had beignets at a famous café.
They are covered in so much powdered sugar that my black T-shirt turned white.
Lily laughed so hard that she spilled her coffee.
In the afternoon, we took a cooking class.
We were taught how to make gumbo, a spicy stew that is made with sausage, shrimp, and vegetables.
“Gumbo was created by many cultures together: African, French, Spanish, and Native American,” the chef explained.
In the evening, we listened to a jazz band in a small club.
An old trumpet player was given a standing ovation after his solo.
Walking back to the hotel, Lily held my hand.
“This is the best birthday I’ve ever had,” she said.
But on the hotel TV, a reporter was talking about a big storm in the Gulf of Mexico.

comp.q: Why did Sam take Lily to New Orleans?
comp.fa: چرا سام لیلی را به نیواورلئان برد؟
چه کسانی نیواورلئان را بنا کردند؟

comp.q: Why did Sam’s T-shirt turn white?
o: It was covered in powdered sugar.

comp.q: According to the chef, who created gumbo?
comp.fa: به گفته‌ی سرآشپز، چه کسانی گامبو را به وجود آوردند؟

comp.q: What does the last sentence suggest?
o: A storm might change their trip.
comp.fa: جمله‌ی آخر چه چیزی را نشان می‌دهد؟
